messages:
ashley: Heads-up — multiple hosted-inference customers reporting 504s and elevated latency since ~02:05 UTC. Saw a spike in gateway 5xx that lines up with cache errors in the gateway logs. Example from gateway: 
``` 
ERROR [gateway/handler.go:234] upstream error: kv: prefix fetch failed: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = redis: read tcp 10.2.8.5:6379: connection reset by peer
WARN  [gateway/cache_pfx.go:87] prefetch fanout failed: 500 responses from cache shard
```
Also seeing memcached timeouts and ‘busy’ responses from cache-proxy. Customers report retries and inflated token usage.

raj: Thanks — can you paste a short repro curl/headers and one full gateway trace? Also which model/route is most affected?

ashley: Repro curl (sanitized):
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer x***" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ \n  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"redwood-large","input":"hello"}'
```
Gateway trace (snip):
```
route=generate model=redwood-large latency=980ms status=504 upstream_err="kv: prefix fetch failed"
cache_shard=shard-12 redis_err="read tcp 10.2.8.5:6379: connection reset by peer"
```
Top symptoms: 504s with KV read errors, short lived but widespread across shards 10-14.

marta: Customers A and B opened support tickets — both hit >7% error rate and complained about token billing spikes due to client retries. They provided logs showing repeated 5xx on first try. Billing team flagged it as possible chargeable incident.

leo: Notable: at 01:58 we rolled a config tweak to prefetch_shards=12 (was 8) to improve warmup for large-seq requests. That rollout went through the gateway canary. Deploy bot: deploy d3f4a7 -> production @ 2026-03-17T01:58Z.

raj: That lines up. Increasing prefetch_shards increases fanout to backend cache and can amplify overloaded redis/memcached pools. Hypothesis: spike in prefetch concurrent connections caused backpressure -> tcp resets and 5xx. Immediate mitigation: revert prefetch_shards to 8, and temporarily enable cache circuit-breaker for heavy routes.

ashley: Quick check — memcached-proxy logs show: 
```
WARN memcached_proxy: conn_pool_exhausted shards=[10,11,12] active=512 limit=500
ERROR memcached_client: io timeout to shard-12
```
Also seeing redis slowlog entries and `OOM command not allowed when used memory > 'maxmemory'` on shard-12.

raj: Ok. Action plan:
  1) Rollback config change (d3f4a7) -> set prefetch_shards=8 (quick rollback).
  2) Short-term: increase cache-proxy conn limit on shard group and enable 429-on-overload to stop retry storms.
  3) Post-mortem: add rate limiter for prefetch fanout and add extra circuit-breaker for heavy routes.

raj: Commands to rollback (run in infra-control):
```
# rollback config map
infractl cfg apply --env prod --set gateway.prefetch_shards=8 --reason "rollback prefetch_shards after cache overload" --owner raj
# trigger rolling restart of cache-proxy on shards 10-14
infractl svc restart cache-proxy --shards 10,11,12,13,14 --parallel 2
```

ashley: Kicking the rollback now. Running first command.

deploy-bot: rollback initiated by ashley for config gateway.prefetch_shards -> 8 (change ID: rback-20260317-01)

ashley: Ran restart on cache-proxy group. Monitoring logs now. Initial errors falling — gateway 5xx rate dropped from 6.8% -> 1.1% over last 3m.

marta: Notifying customers: will update tickets with mitigation and workaround. Also asking billing to hold any contested charges until we finish triage.

raj: Please capture:
  - exact time rollback applied (for incident timeline)
  - pre/post metrics for cache connection saturation and gateway 5xx rates
  - list of affected shards and any redis OOM traces
I’ll file a follow-up RFC to add prefetch fanout safeguards.

ashley: Timeline notes:
  - 01:58Z deploy d3f4a7 (prefetch_shards=12)
  - 02:05Z error spike detected in prod (first customer report)
  - 02:12Z rollback rback-20260317-01 applied
  - 02:17Z cache-proxy rolling restarts started
  - 02:22Z 5xx rates dropped to ~1%

sre-bot: alert cleared for gateway-5xx-high at 02:25Z (duration 20m).

marta: Putting immediate workaround in support KB: advise customers to retry with exponential backoff and enable client-side token limits. Also adding note that transient retries during cache overload may cause token inflation.

ashley: :thumbsup: Will attach logs and grep output to the incident ticket.

raj: Next steps: postmortem, add metric for prefetch_fanout_active_connections, and implement circuit-breaker behavior: return 503/429 quickly for cache overload instead of letting gateway accumulate retries.

marta: Opening incident ticket and will coordinate follow-up with billing and customers. Thanks all. :heart:
